group.passage:
Every year, millions of people buy new phones, laptops, and tablets, often long before their old ones stop working. Because companies release new models so often, a phone bought just two years ago can already seem [[1]]. Some people upgrade simply because they want the latest features, not because anything is wrong with the devices they already have. The result is a massive, fast-growing pile of electronic waste, or “e-waste.”
Yet old electronics are not just [[2]] to be thrown away. A typical phone contains small amounts of [[3]] metals such as gold, silver, and copper. In fact, some experts describe piles of unwanted devices as an “urban [[4]]” that is waiting to be dug. At the same time, many devices also contain [[5]] substances like lead and mercury. When e-waste is buried in ordinary landfills, these chemicals can slowly [[6]] into the soil and water nearby, where they may contaminate crops and drinking water.
Recycling could solve part of the problem, yet only a small share of the world’s e-waste is collected and recycled properly. Many old devices [[7]] in poorer countries instead, where workers, including some children, burn plastic-coated wires to get at the copper inside. The fumes from these fires are a serious health [[8]] for the workers and their neighbors.
Experts say the simplest solution is to keep devices in use for longer. Replacing a worn-out battery or a cracked screen can [[9]] a phone’s useful life by years. Many products, however, are hard to fix because their parts are glued together. In response, a growing “right to repair” movement is calling on companies to make repairs easier. Before throwing out an old device, it is also worth asking whether it could be fixed, passed on to someone else, or [[10]] at a proper recycling center.

1.explanation_zh: can already seem ___ 需要形容詞（seem＋adj.）。because 子句說廠商推出新機型的速度太快，所以才買兩年的手機就「像老古董一樣」；ancient 原指「古代的」，這裡是誇飾的延伸用法，強調「非常過時」。precious、toxic 雖是形容詞，但和「新機型推出太快」的原因接不上。
evidence: Because companies release new models so often, a phone bought just two years ago can already seem [[1]].

option_notes_zh.D: end up（片語動詞，最後落得、最後到了（某處））詞性不合：空格在 can already seem 之後，需要形容詞。
option_notes_zh.E: mine（名詞，礦場、礦坑（也可當代名詞「我的」））詞性不合：空格在 can already seem 之後，需要形容詞。
option_notes_zh.F: a phone can already seem toxic（手機看起來有毒）不合因果；toxic 屬於第 5 格。
option_notes_zh.G: extend（動詞，延長）詞性不合：空格在 can already seem 之後，需要形容詞。

1.strategy_zh: seem 後面接形容詞；由「新機型推出太快」推出舊手機顯得「過時」，ancient 在這裡是誇飾。

The result is a massive, fast-growing pile of electronic waste, or “e-waste.”

translation_zh.text:
每年都有數百萬人購買新的手機、筆電和平板，常常在舊的還沒壞之前就換掉了。因為廠商推出新機型的速度太快，才買兩年的手機看起來就已經像老古董。有些人換新機只是因為想要最新的功能，並不是手上的裝置出了什麼問題。結果，電子廢棄物（也就是「電子垃圾」）堆積如山，而且增加得非常快。
然而，舊電子產品並不只是要丟掉的垃圾。一支普通的手機裡含有少量的金、銀、銅等貴金屬。事實上，有些專家把成堆的廢棄裝置形容成等待開挖的「城市礦山」。同時，許多裝置也含有鉛、汞等有毒物質。電子垃圾被埋進一般的掩埋場時，這些化學物質會慢慢滲入附近的土壤和水中，可能污染農作物和飲用水。
回收可以解決部分問題，但全世界的電子垃圾只有一小部分被妥善收集與回收。許多舊裝置反而流落到較貧窮的國家，在那裡，工人（其中包括一些兒童）焚燒包著塑膠的電線，以取出裡面的銅。燒電線產生的有毒煙霧，對工人和他們的鄰居都是嚴重的健康危害。
專家表示，最簡單的解決辦法就是讓裝置用得更久。換掉老舊的電池或破裂的螢幕，就能讓手機的使用壽命延長好幾年。然而，許多產品的零件是用膠黏在一起的，很難修理。為此，越來越多人加入「維修權」運動，呼籲廠商讓維修變得更容易。在丟掉舊裝置之前，也值得問問自己：它能不能修理、送給別人，或拿到正規的回收中心？
